questions.question: In which of the following years did Pandit Bhimsen Gururaj Joshi give his first ever live performance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1941.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandit Bhimsen** Joshi first performed live in **1941** at the age of 19.
 
• His debut album, **containing a few devotional songs in Marathi and Hindi, was released by HMV the next year in 1942.**
 
• Later Joshi moved to Mumbai in 1943 and** worked as a radio artist.**
 
• His performance at a** concert in 1946 **to celebrate his** guru Sawai Gandharva's 60th birthday won him accolades both from the audience and his guru.**

 [IMAGE: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/91/ShashankwithBhimsenJoshi.jpg/220px-ShashankwithBhimsenJoshi.jpg] 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **​**His first music teacher was **Channappa of Kurtakoti,** who had trained with the **veteran singer Inayat Khan.**
 
• Joshi heard a recording of **Abdul Karim Khan's Thumri "Piya Bin Nahi Aavat Chain" in Raga Jhinjhoti**** when he was a child, which inspired him to become a musician.**
 
• During this time, he also **heard Pandit ****Sawai Gandharva at a performance in Kundgol. In 1933, the 11-year-old Joshi left Dharwad for Bijapur**** to find a master's and learn music.**

questions.question: ‘The Life Divine’, ‘The Synthesis of Yoga’ and ‘Savitri’ are the popular works of which of the following extremist freedom fighters of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aurobindo Ghosh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Aurobindo Ghosh was an **Indian philosopher**, yogi, guru, poet, and nationalist.
 
• He was one of the influential leaders in the early part of the Indian independence movement.
 
• His notable works include '**The Life Divine**', '**The Synthesis of Yoga**', and '**Savitri**'.
 
• He later moved to Pondicherry and founded the Aurobindo Ashram, dedicating his life to spiritual practice and writing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Extremist Freedom Fighters:**

 
 
• Extremist freedom fighters believed in more radical approaches to achieve independence from British rule.
 
• They often advocated for direct action, including protests, boycotts, and sometimes even armed struggle.
 
• Prominent extremist leaders included **Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, and Lala Lajpat Rai**, collectively known as the Lal-Bal-Pal trio.
 
 
 
• **Aurobindo Ghosh's Contribution to Indian Freedom Movement:**
 
 
• Aurobindo was initially involved in the Indian freedom struggle and was a member of the Indian National Congress.
 
• He was associated with the revolutionary activities and was arrested in the **Alipore Bomb Case in 1908**, though later acquitted.
 
• After his acquittal, Aurobindo gradually retreated from active politics and focused on spiritual and philosophical pursuits.
 
 
 
• **The Life Divine:**
 
 
• This is a book written by Aurobindo Ghosh that expounds on his philosophical ideas and spiritual experiences.
 
• It addresses the nature of reality, the evolution of consciousness, and the ultimate goal of human life.
 
 
 
• **The Synthesis of Yoga:**
 
 
• Another significant work by Aurobindo, it elaborates on the integration of various paths of yoga (such as** Karma Yoga, Bhakti Yoga, and Jnana Yoga**) into a comprehensive spiritual practice.
 
 
 
• **Savitri:**
 
 
• An epic **poem **written by Aurobindo, it is considered one of his masterpieces and is based on the **legend of Savitri and Satyavan **from the **Mahabharata**.
 
• The poem explores themes of **human destiny, love, and transformation**.

questions.question: In Kheda, Gujarat, Patidar peasants organised non-violent campaigns against which of the following demand of the British?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __High land revenue__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Patidar peasants in Kheda, Gujarat, organized non-violent campaigns against the British primarily** due to their demand for** high land revenue.**
 
• This was** one of the key issues that led to the Kheda Satyagraha of 1918, **a significant event in the **Indian independence movement, which was led by figures like Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi, Vallabhbhai Patel, and others.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Kheda Satyagraha__

 
 
• In the middle of the Kheda Satyagraha (1918), Gandhi also got involved in the Ahmedabad textile mill strike.
 
• Here his adversaries were the Gujarati millowners.
 
• The immediate reason for the industrial conflict was the withdrawal of plague bonus, which was being given to dissuade workers from leaving the city in the face of mounting plague-related deaths.
 
• Also, it was during Ahmedabad textile mill strike that Gandhiji for the first time during the Indian National Movement took fast unto death( to strengthen the workers‘ resolve).
 
• Hence his first hunger strike was during Ahmedabad Strike and not at Kheda.
 
• The cause for Kheda Satyagraha was that the peasants of Kheda district were in extreme distress due to a failure of crops and that their appeals for the remission of land revenue were being ignored by the Government.
 
• Discontinuation of the Plague bonus was the immediate cause for Ahmedabad textile mill strike.

questions.question: Who founded the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) in Calcutta?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__ **"Prasantha Chandra Mahalanobis".**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Indian Statistical Institute is a public research university.
 
• The motto of this institute is** " Unity in Diversity".**
 
• The headquarter of this institute is** Bonhoogly ( Baranagar), Kolkata, West Bengal.**
 
• It has four subsidiary centres in **Delhi, Bengal, Chennai, and Giridih.**
 
• The primary activities of ISI are research and training of Statistics, development of theoretical statistics, and its application.
 
• ISI comes under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation of the government of India.
 
• Founded by Professor P.C. Mahalanobis in **Kolkata on 17th December 1931, **the institute gained the status of an Institution of National Importance by an act of the Indian Parliament in 1959.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The key areas of expertise of** ISI are -**

 
• **Statistics**
 
• **Computer science**
 
• **Mathematics**
 
• **Operation Research**
 
• **Information science.**

questions.question: Who was best known for hoisting the Indian National Congress flag at the Gowalia Tank maidan in Bombay during the Quit India Movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**" Aruna Asaf Ali ".**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Aruna Asaf Ali was a political activist and participated in the Indian Independence movement.
 
• She is known for hoisting the Indian flag at the Gowalia Tank Maidan in Mumbai during the Quit India Movement.
 
• In 1958, She also became **" Delhi's first mayor ".**
 
• Aruna Asaf Ali is popularly known as the '**Grand Old Lady**' of the Independence Movement.
 
• **Gowalia Tank Maidan** is located in central Mumbai.
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi** issue the quit India speech in this garden.
 
• She was greatly influenced by **Mahatma Gandhi's ideas and beliefs.**
 
• In 1932, she had gone on a hunger strike in **Tihar Jail **against the mistreatment of the political prisoners

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• **She got the following awards -**

 
 
• International Lenin peace prize in 1964
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru Prize in 1991
 
• Padma Vibhushan in 1992
 
• Bharat Ratna in 1997.

questions.question: In which year was the Chicago (USA) Conference of World Religions held that included Swami Vivekananda's talk on religion as one of its highlights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 4) i.e. __1893__.**

__
 
• The **1893 **__World’s Parliament of Religions was held on the shore of **Lake Michigan, Chicago **was the largest and most spectacular event among many other congresses.
 
• The World Congress of Religions marks the first formal gathering of representatives of Eastern and Western spiritual traditions.
 
• **Swami Vivekananda** mesmerized the 5,000 assembled delegates, greeting them with the words, **“Sisters and brothers of America!” **
 
• This speech, which introduced** Hinduism to America** is memorized by school children in India to this day.
 
• Swami Vivekananda became one of the most forceful and popular speakers in spite of the fact that he had never before addressed an audience in public.
 
• 19 women spoke at this Parliament, an unprecedented occurrence until 1893.
